title: Hybrid Identity: AD to Microsoft Entra
built: Extended an existing AD lab with scoped directory synchronization and Windows 11 hybrid join.
problem: Connect on-premises identities to a cloud directory while preserving administrator separation and service access after guest restarts.
objective: Synchronize the twelve standard departmental users and the owned workstation, verify hybrid join and real-user PRT, and document protected access persistence.
outcome: 23/23 acceptance checks passed. Twelve users synchronized; exact cloud device enabled with ServerAd trust. Both joins, successful device authentication and standard-user PRT verified after client restart. Sync service resumed automatically after server restart.
steps: Read the [chronological build story](evidence/BUILD-STORY.md) for the complete implementation and troubleshooting sequence.
Follow the [illustrated manual reproduction walkthrough](evidence/MANUAL.md), including installation, OU filtering, staging, SCP discovery, activation and verification.
Review [protected access and persistence](evidence/PERSISTENT-ACCESS.md); human authentication, the delegated cache and the sync service identity are separate.

tests.check: all eight unrelated guest configurations unchanged
privileged administrator account kept cloud only
client join and sso after restart
sync service returned after dc restart without desktop login
protected admin cache reused from fresh process

problems: Client NAT adapter disabled at PnP level; enabled the identified device and used a scoped static guest NAT address after DHCP left APIPA.
Multihomed DC published unwanted NAT DNS addresses; restricted listening/publishing and authoritative records to the private LAN.
Older download links returned HTML; rejected unsigned payloads and used the signed Microsoft Connect MSI.
Machine trust required owned machine-password repair; refreshed native Netlogon verification before evaluating a stale PowerShell result.
Source-anchor writes needed the next delta confirmation; final pending exports were zero on both connectors.
Authentication metadata collection raced an asynchronous refresh; collected completed fresh-process status before final acceptance.

limitations: Original implementation evidence, captured October 22 local / October 23 UTC; publication does not rerun the lab. Host reboot, browser application SSO and licensed Office access were not tested. PRT verification demonstrates user SSO token acquisition, not app access. Public scripts and placeholder instructions were not independently replayed. One implementation platform tested. Connect installed on the DC for this small training lab; production placement and capacity require a separate design. Password and MFA prompts are intentionally excluded from screenshots. Cloud-only administrator retained; no Windows automatic login configured.
